messages.author: adc8ca6cfb4e05df
messages.subject: segfault following DATA_STRUCT example
parts:
Follow the example here but could not figure out what's wrong

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/group__macros.html#gaf9885566da0d248c1a4b4d7a0eeafcd2

I have this R code
library(TMB)
compile("tst.cpp")
dyn.load(dynlib("tst"))
data <- list()
data$object <- list(a=1:10, b=matrix(1:6,2))
parameters <- list(c = 1, d = 212312)
ob <- TMB::MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL="tst", silent=0)

and tst.cpp

#include <TMB.hpp>
template<class Type>
struct my_list {
  vector<Type> a;
  matrix<Type> b;
  my_list(SEXP x){ // Constructor
    a = asVector<Type>(getListElement(x,"a"));
    b = asMatrix<Type>(getListElement(x,"b"));
  }
};
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() () {
    DATA_STRUCT(object, my_list);
    return 0;
}
Compiler's message
/usr/local/clang8/bin/clang++ -fopenmp -isysroot /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk -I"/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/include" -DNDEBUG -I"/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library/TMB/include"   -DTMB_SAFEBOUNDS -DLIB_UNLOAD=R_unload_tst  -DTMB_LIB_INIT=R_init_tst   -I/usr/local/include   -fPIC  -Wall -g -O2  -c tst.cpp -o tst.o
Abort
 ob <- TMB::MakeADFun(data, parameters, DLL="tst", silent=0)
Order of parameters:
[1] "c" "d"
Not matching template order:
character(0)
Your parameter list has been re-ordered.
(Disable this warning with checkParameterOrder=FALSE)
0 regions found.
Using 1 threads
TMB has received an error from Eigen. The following condition was not met:
index >= 0 && index < size()
Please check your matrix-vector bounds etc., or run your program through a debugger.
Abort trap: 6

messages.author: 5f950c9713997d19
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] segfault following DATA_STRUCT example
parts:
Hi Kinh

I ran the example and replicated your error. I then inserted PARMETER(c); and PARAMETER(d); into the cpp file as per 

     ...
    DATA_STRUCT(object, my_list);
    PARAMETER(c);
    PARAMETER(d);
    REPORT(object.a);
    ...
    
The example ran as expected with ob$report() created as a list of 2 ($object.a and $object.b). 

The conflict appears to be the explicit lack of Parameter definition in the cpp file.

Bob

Another user suggested me to do the same but somehow I did not get it to work. It does now. Thanks both!

After a few more tries I think that we had to read at least one parameter for it not to crash, which was not what I expected as all PARAMETER() does is just read and make a parameter name available from R’s SEXP.
